bugs.summary: should recursive package dependencies be checked in install.packages()?
bugs.creator: kevinushey

comments.text:
In particular, if one attempts to install a package whose _immediate_ dependencies are installed, but _recursive_ dependencies are not installed, install.packages() will not install the missing recursive dependencies.

This can be demonstrated with the CRAN package 'abc', which currently indirectly depends on SparseM through the dependency chain:

    abc -> quantreg -> SparseM

To reproduce:
    
    templib <- tempfile()
    dir.create(templib)
    .libPaths(templib)
    
    install.packages("abc", lib = templib)
    remove.packages("SparseM", lib = templib)
    remove.packages("abc", lib = templib)
    install.packages("abc", lib = templib)
    library(abc, lib = templib)

Note that, on the second attempt to install 'abc', 'SparseM' was not installed, and so could not be loaded.

Note that this example is artificial, in that we had to forcefully remove a required sub-package. However, we've seen things like this happen in the wild, especially when e.g. a mixture of packages get installed into different libraries (although I don't have the exact steps one might take to reproduce this in a more natural way).

comments.text:
Tried the example under R 4.5.0 and the result differs slightly from before; at the point of:

> install.packages("abc", lib = templib)

it now directly gives

  Error: package 'SparseM' required by 'quantreg' could not be found
  Execution halted
  ERROR: lazy loading failed for package 'abc'

For what that's worth...
